results.summary_before: This design is a UART receiver that watches for the ASCII string MARCO and, upon detecting it, replies with a carriage-return and newline wrapped POLO! and toggles a WS2812B LED from red to green. It runs at 50 MHz with 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity and one stop bit, and exposes debug signals for the baud ticks, transmit trigger and busy flag. Testing requires a USB-to-TTL adapter and a WS2812B LED, and the author reports it was verified on an FPGA. It is a small, self-contained demonstration of UART plus addressable-LED driving.

results.summary_before: This project implements a Direct Memory Access (DMA) controller that processes transfer descriptors from a ring buffer, configured over SPI. It includes an SPI register interface, a ring manager, a descriptor fetcher and data mover, and an interrupt output for ring-empty and error conditions. The design is tested by connecting an external SPI master and writing configuration and descriptor tail pointer registers; internal activity is monitored via probe outputs. For this tapeout, an internal memory stub replaces an AXI4 master, and no external hardware beyond an SPI master is required. The design is notable for its autonomous descriptor processing and consolidated interrupt scheme.

results.summary_before: This design counts seconds and displays the value on a 7-segment display, with the lower counter bits also available on the bidirectional pins. The input pins program a 24-bit compare register so the counting rate can be changed from the default one-second interval. It is a standard Tiny Tapeout Verilog demo intended to show clock division and binary-to-decimal conversion. The documentation is complete and describes both the default and programmable counting behavior.
